問い 3: sink 語彙・入口規則・weak 理由の追加を求める所見ではない（帰属規則 §2.9 (b) の実装の話）。§2 の除外に当たらない。
問い 4: D1（追記型 FS_WRITE が新たに矛になる = 主指標 (ユニット, site, kind) が増える）と D2 → D1 の宣言列の移動（contradiction_by_decl / contradictions.json の declarations）に効くので「記録のみ」ではない。

design.reason: This behaviour was not an intended decision. No record in decisions / open_questions / preregistration / the spec / D19 K1-K7 / review_plan §5 names the same root cause, which is the reversed condition in pass (1) of `_self_fields`. In analyze.py:351-352, `if not name.startswith("self.")` followed by `name[len("self."):]` takes every name bound in the class body and drops its first 5 characters to make a fabricated field. It is the opposite of the (2) `__init__` loop (`if name.startswith("self.")`), which is plainly the model it was copied from, so it is a transcription error. The design records point the other way. D35 (b) (decisions.md:280) and the spec (AUTHGAP_BRIEF_v3.md:1198) say class-body defaults go into the fields as they are and `__init__` overwrites them, which requires reading `self.sql` as the class attribute `sql`. Rereading the expected output from the rules: in Python semantics `self.sql` is `Store.sql = "DELETE FROM items"`. So under contradiction_principles.md §7.1 (DB: SQL_MODIFY_HEADS → contradiction, D55), Store.purge should be `contradiction:D1 db_modify`, the same as Store2.purge2. The finding's expected output matches the rules. In the path example the D1 verdict is FS_READ → consistent under either reading, but the fabricated value can reach the path of a write (D2) or a URL. This is not a vocabulary issue and does not touch any freeze. It is a flaw in receiver inference (the heap seed). The class-body `self` binding also leaves a stray '' field, and a fabricated resolved constant can hide a field that is only bound lazily, which risks false-clean. The fix (delete pass (1)) is correct in general: nothing but a Name target is bound in a class body, so pass (1) produces nothing that is not fabricated. Pass (2) (analyze.py:353-360) already puts in the correct class attributes.
design.notes: It needs a name collision with a 5-character prefix (base_/data_/root_/host_ etc. + the name of another attribute read through self, with no `__init__` assignment), so it is rare. But it comes up with pydantic-style tools that declare their fields in the class body, and it hits method-form units (the `_self_fields` seed) directly. Depending on which way the fabrication goes it gives either false-clean or a false alarm. The root cause is separate from R4-r2-5 / R4-r2-6 (missing base classes / lazy binding).

The proxy catalogue in spec Def 3(b) fixes the method as `*`: `git.Repo(p).git.*` / `git.cmd.Git.*` → `SPAWN { argv0 ← "git", argv[*] ← *args, cwd ← p, shell ← False }` (AUTHGAP_BRIEF_v3.md:227). The proxy rows are part of the month-3 sink vocabulary freeze (AUTHGAP_BRIEF_v3.md:841, 'sink vocabulary (direct + proxy + pipe ...)'). sinks.py:452-463 (`method="*"`) and the constant 'git' injection at effects.py:725-728 transcribe that row directly. Applying §7.1 SPAWN ('argv0 or shell_string from MODEL → contradiction / otherwise → unknown'), every method that hits the frozen row has argv0 = constant 'git', so `contradiction_unknown:D1:spawn_command` is the rule-conformant result. The finding's expected output (no SPAWN row for update_environment and friends) needs an exclusion set carved out of the `*` in the frozen proxy row. That is a change to the frozen sink vocabulary: not an addition, but a narrowing of the row's range. Under CLAUDE.md rule 5 ('items the spec marks frozen are not changed based on results seen after the freeze') it belongs in the same category as O39 (the frozen vocabulary is coarser than the real API). I am being consistent with the design-lens verdict on R4-r3-4 (the other defect in the same `*` field), which was refuted for the same reason (verify_r3plus_R2R4R5.json). Doubt (why confidence is only 0.6): the spec's `*` was probably written with the `__getattr__` form (subcommands such as `repo.git.checkout`) in mind, and it is unlikely that explicit non-spawning methods like `custom_environment` / `update_environment` / `clear_cache` were included deliberately. So there is room to read this as 'a vocabulary entry applied too broadly (a matching error)' rather than 'a vocabulary addition'. Even so, the direction is inside → unknown, which does not create a contradiction, and when a tool also runs a real git command (the common case with custom_environment) the unit-level verdict does not change.
